target.family: n>=5, S={1,...,n-1}\{r1,r2}, 1<=r1<r2<n, n<=w1<w2, all phases zero
target.scope: All deletion positions; no primitive-gcd hypothesis; cover hypothesis includes strict counterexamples and equality.

method: Five focused fresh web searches, then primary-source theorem/proof reading. No general web-source paraphrase was accepted as a substitute for the primary statement. Exact inspected locations and scope comparisons are below.

sources.title: Barely lonely runners and very lonely runners
sources.author: Noah Kravitz
sources.statement: Proposition 8.1: if a prefix with largest speed v has loneliness at least L, adding a speed at least ((L-epsilon)/epsilon)*v leaves loneliness at least L-epsilon. Lemma 8.4: for m final moving speeds and prefix loneliness greater than 1/m, a new speed at least v*(2*v-1) yields loneliness at least 1/m. Lemma 8.5 gives a linear-in-v cutoff under the preceding-dimensional Spectrum Conjecture.
sources.comparison: The quadratic cutoff is in the previous largest speed, not the runner-count parameter. In our target there are n-1 moving speeds and the proved prefix margin is above 1/n, which does not supply the printed Lemma 8.4 premise above 1/(n-1). Proposition 8.1 can be adapted at threshold 1/n, but this alone does not supply a uniform O(n^2) bound for arbitrary two deletions; prefix margins or the new source-specific geometry remain necessary. Its non-strict conclusion also requires care for a target cover at equality. This is clear methodological prior and should not be presented as a new fast-runner principle.

sources.version: Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 180 (2026), 343–361; first published online 24 October 2025; DOI 10.1017/S0305004125101497
sources.title: The structure of Lonely Runner spectra
sources.statement: A geometric argument gives an explicit finite checking bound for the general Lonely Runner Conjecture, conditional on the preceding dimension; the displayed sufficient volume threshold uses epsilon=1/(m*(m+1)) and the volume of the (m-1)-dimensional unit ball. The stated growth bound is below m^((5/2)*m).
sources.comparison: This is a general conditional finite checking result, not an unconditional quadratic bound in n for every cover obtained by replacing two entries of [n-1]. Qualitative finiteness and finite multiplicity do not supply the claimed family-specific exponent or constants.

sources.version: arXiv:2411.12684v2, 9 December 2024; published Combinatorial Theory 6(1) (2026), paper 1
sources.title: Relative Lonely Runner spectra
sources.statement: For a fixed proper two-dimensional subtorus, the relative one-dimensional spectrum differs by finitely many elements from a finite union of rational arithmetic-progression reciprocal families above its base distance.
sources.comparison: This is a fixed-subtorus structural description with finite exceptional sets, not an explicit uniform runner-count quadratic cutoff for our arbitrary two inserted speeds. Allowing both insertions independently along with the retained baseline direction naturally gives three generating directions, so the two-dimensional theorem does not directly settle the whole target family.

sources.title: Odd denominators in the Lonely Runner spectrum for six speeds
sources.author: Francesco Cordella
sources.statement: Theorem 5.3 gives maximum speed below 3q on the specified six-speed critical subtorus U_C for near-tight primitive tuples with reduced loneliness denominator q. Question 6.6 asks about a universal six-speed 3q bound and discusses general bounds with dimension-dependent C(m), finite exceptions, and lower-dimensional LRC assumptions.
sources.comparison: The theorem is fixed dimension and a specified subtorus, while the general discussion retains conditional assumptions, unspecified dimension dependence, or finite exceptions. It does not immediately yield the unrestricted two-deletion O(n^2) cutoff for all n.

conclusion: No inspected primary statement directly implies the unrestricted two-entry quadratic bound in the runner-count parameter. Kravitz Proposition 8.1 is direct methodological prior for fast-runner perturbation; Lemma 8.4 is a true quadratic bound in a different parameter with a different threshold premise. The repository must retain its scoped and unverified academic-priority status.
